newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/MCI options busy before talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/MCI options busy before talks.

text.p: Investors were buying MCI Communications Corp November calls ahead of news Friday it was in talks with British Telecommunications Plc on a possible combination, traders said.
But analysts and traders said it was not clear whether insider trading had taken place.
"We've seen increased activity in the options over the last week, mostly on the buy side of the calls," said a trader in Chicago, where MCI options trade.
"It continued through today," he said.
By late afternoon, about 2,465 of the MCI November 30 calls changed hands. The option, with open interest of 427, was up 3-1/4 at 3-1/2.
The January 30 call, up 1-9/16 at 2-1/4, traded 1,445 on open interest of 2,929.
Other active MCI options included the November 22-1/2 call, the November 25 call and the December 27-1/2 call. The most active put was the November 25, which traded 618.
The trader in Chicago said it was not clear whether the earlier call buying was just on speculation of a possible deal or from someone with knowledge of it.
He said volatilities in the November calls had risen sharply.
"You can be suspicious but there's very little data to prove anything," said Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, referring to the recent action in the MCI November 30 calls.
Over the last five trading sessions, the November 30 call traded 25, 80, 75, nil and 282 contracts respectively.
Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, added that activity in the November 25 calls was also not significant.
"It doesn't look like (insider trading) to me," he said.
MCI shares had rallied early Friday on talk that either BT or GTE Corp would buy the company.
After MCI shares were halted for news pending, the company confirmed it was in talks with BT on a possible combination. BT already owns 20 percent of MCI.
The last sale in MCI shares before the Nasdaq halt was 27-1/4, up 1-7/8. It had reached a session high of 31.
Nasdaq said it would evaluate the validity of all trades in MCI that appeared to have been made after the stock was halted at 1227 CST (1827 GMT).
Traders in Chicago said the options stopped trading as soon as the stock was halted.
ADRs of BT fell two to 55-5/8 on the news, drawing a little options interest.
The BT November 55 put, with open interest of 25, traded 1,035 contracts. It rose 1-3/16 to 1-3/8. The corresponding call, with open interest of eight, traded 920 contracts. It fell 5/8 to 2-1/8.
